result.noFurtherDiscriminator: All 6 turns have been observed. The pattern is consistent: the team is capacity-blocked at command-deck from turn 1 onward, never successfully moves again, and never engages the hive. No unobserved turn remains that could discriminate between the alternatives — the evidence is exhausted.
result.rationale: The rescue team is pinned at command-deck for all 6 turns. In turn 1, both engineer-imani and medic-reyes attempt to move to junction-cover but are contested with "target_zone_capacity_lost" — the zone they need to reach is capacity-blocked. After that, the team never attempts another move; all three actors repeatedly issue "guard:command-deck" (no_effect, no_hostile_movement_triggered) from turns 2-5. The hive-alpha moves freely (life-console, life-duct, life-entry) while the team is stuck. Meanwhile reactor-heat climbs 62→100, oxygen 68→42, battery 48→36 — a mounting survival/spatial pressure clock. The team's only attack attempt (pirate-captain-veyra's scatter-blast) was invalidated as target_out_of_range_after_movement, and the rescue team itself never attacks at all. The core bottleneck is that the actors cannot reach the zones where the hive/affordances are located because zone capacity blocks their movement, and the resulting spatial pressure (heat/oxygen drain) compounds. This is a survival-spatial-pressure pattern: hostile/zone-capacity pressure blocks the actor before the useful affordance (engaging hive-alpha, reaching junction-cover) becomes actionable.
